highlights: EU Council & Parliament agreed (7 May 2026, 'Omnibus VII') to delay high-risk AI obligations to 2 Dec 2027 (standalone) and 2 Aug 2028 (product-embedded); new ban on non-consensual sexual/intimate content & CSAM.
EU AI Act Complaint Tool and Whistleblower Tool are already live (EU page last updated 3 Aug 2026) — citizens can report suspected violations now.

AlgorithmWatch 'Automating Injustice' report (28 Mar 2025) maps predictive-policing systems in Germany; individual criminal-risk prediction is banned under the AI Act but many systems reportedly lack a legal basis.
CJEU C-634/21 (7 Dec 2023): credit scores are automated decisions under Art. 22 GDPR — citizens may demand logic info and contest solely automated decisions.
Jobcenters received 501,667 appeals in 2025 (+78,310); 30–40% of appeals succeed, signalling frequent automated-notice errors; BVerfG 5 Nov 2019 limited blanket sanctions.
